newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling continues rally against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling continues rally against dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling continued its rally against the dollar on Tuesday, posting new highs as exporter sales from tea and coffee flowed into the market, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean of 55.35 shillings to the dollar from 55.40 on Thursday, while sterling was posted at 92.92 shillings, down from 93.29.
"Exporter sales permeated the market, sending rates below the 55.40 level," a dealer said.
Dealers said the market was active on Tuesday morning, with much buying through the interbank market. This new demand saw the shilling lose marginally, trading at 55.39/38 levels at midmorning.

"A lot of today's demand has come in from importers who have been monitoring the shilling," Phillip Wambua, an assistant chief dealer at Banque Indosuez said. "We really cannot tell which sector is buying," he added.
"Oil importers have interest in buying dollars at these levels," another dealer said.
Some dealers said the 55.00 barrier looked like the next psychological point. They expressed optimism in the shilling, anticipating a weaker greenback in time.
The money market was liquid with many banks looking for money. Overnight rates were pushed up to 10 percent levels from below 10 percent levels on Thursday.
-- Wambui Chege, Nairobi Newsroom ++254-2 330-261 REUTER WMC
